source_title: Cabinet approves ₹10,000 crore scheme to boost container manufacturing - Business Standard
source_excerpt: Following Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman’s Budget announcement in February, the Cabinet on Wednesday approved the ₹10,000 crore Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme (CMPS), which aims to make India a competitive market for this important cog of the global trade wheel. The scheme, which will provide financial support to India’s nascent container manufacturers, will run till 2039-40 (FY40). With the scheme, the Centre intends to increase annual domestic container manufacturing capacity by around ten-fold, up to 750,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs). It also sees potential to position India as a global export hub for quality shipping containers. The scheme is expected to generate an estimated 3,000 direct jobs and over 50,000 indirect jobs, while supporting ancillary industries such as corner castings, specialised steel, wooden frames and paints. India’s traders have suffered from high freight costs in the wake of global crises from as early as 2023 — with container leasing and buying rates turning volatile. Global shipping lines also procured containers largely from China, owing to major cost advantages. According to industry sources, there’s a substantial difference between an India-manufactured container and one manufactured in China. For one TEU, a Chinese container is available for around $1,700, compared with around $2,200-2,400 for others, according to one manufacturer. The scheme aims to bridge these gaps and will offer interest subvention (ISA) with a financial outlay of ₹859 crore to provide assistance of 3 per cent per annum on eligible term loans (capital loans) availed by companies for setting up greenfield container manufacturing facilities and brownfield expansion of existing capacities. The scheme will also provide an operational expenditure assistance (OEA) with a financial outlay of ₹8,891 crore to provide support for all containers manufactured as per global shipping standards and sold by eligible container manufacturers. “This would help bridge the cost gap and improve the competitiveness of domestically manufactured containers,” the Cabinet statement said. The government hopes that the continued assistance will allow steelmakers to build capacity to produce specialty steel required for containers at a lower price. The scheme also provides testing and certification assistance with a financial outlay of ₹150 crore to support setting up of common facilities such as dynamic longitudinal impact testing. Since the announcement of the scheme, infrastructure giants like Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone have reportedly expressed interest in building boxes in India. Danish Shipping Line Maersk also placed its first order on an Indian manufacturer, DCM Containers and Engineering, earlier this year. hi_body:
भारत के कब्‍ब्‍य ने ₹10,000 करोड़ का कंटेनर निर्माण प्रचार योजना (CMPS) मंज़ूर की है, जिसका उद्देश्य भारत को वैश्विक कंटेनर बाजार में प्रतिस्पर्धी बनाना है। यह योजना, वित्त मंत्री नर्मला सीतारामन के फरवरी बजट के बाद, FY 2039‑40 तक चलेगी और वार्षिक घरेलू कंटेनर उत्पादन क्षमता को दस गुना बढ़ाकर 750,000 टेफ (TEUs) तक पहुँचाने का लक्ष्य रखती है।

CMPS की प्रमुख विशेषताएँ:
- **ब्याज सब्सिडी (ISA)**: ₹859 करोड़ को नई ग्रीनफ़ील्ड संयंत्रों की स्थापना या मौजूदा सुविधाओं के विस्तार के लिए टर्म लोन पर 3 % वार्षिक ब्याज सब्सिडी के रूप में आवंटित किया जाएगा।
- **संचालन व्यय सहायता (OEA)**: ₹8,891 करोड़ को वैश्विक शिपिंग मानकों के अनुसार निर्मित और योग्य निर्माताओं द्वारा बेचे जाने वाले कंटेनरों के संचालन लागत का समर्थन करने के लिए इस्तेमाल किया जाएगा।
- **परीक्षण एवं प्रमाणन सहायता**: ₹150 करोड़ को डायनामिक लॉन्गिट्यूडिनल इम्पैक्ट टेस्टिंग जैसी सामान्य परीक्षण सुविधाओं के निर्माण के लिए फंड किया जाएगा।

इस योजना से लगभग 3,000 प्रत्यक्ष नौकरियाँ और 50,000 से अधिक अप्रत्यक्ष नौकरियाँ पैदा होने की उम्मीद है, साथ ही कोने के कास्टिंग, विशेष स्टील, लकड़ी के फ्रेम और पेंट जैसी सहायक उद्योगों को भी लाभ होगा। भारतीय और चीनी कंटेनरों के बीच लागत अंतर को पाटने के लिए यह योजना बनाई गई है—चीनी TEU की कीमत $1,700 है, जबकि भारतीय TEU की कीमत $2,200‑$2,400 के बीच है।

उद्योग की प्रतिक्रिया सकारात्मक रही है। अडानी पोर्ट्स और विशेष आर्थिक क्षेत्र ने भारत में कंटेनर निर्माण में रुचि व्यक्त की है, और डेनिश शिपिंग लाइन मर्स्क ने इस वर्ष की शुरुआत में भारतीय निर्माता DCM कंटेनर्स एंड इंजीनियरिंग से पहला ऑर्डर दिया।

**सत्यापन कैसे करें**: योजना के विवरण कब्‍ब्‍य के प्रेस रिलीज़ में प्रकाशित हैं और उन्हें वाणिज्य व उद्योग मंत्रालय की आधिकारिक वेबसाइट पर जाँचा जा सकता है। सहायता चाहने वाली कंपनियों को मंत्रालय द्वारा जारी योजना दिशानिर्देशों से परामर्श करना चाहिए।

en_body:
The Indian Cabinet has sanctioned a ₹10,000‑crore Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme (CMPS) to make India a competitive player in the global container market. The scheme, announced after Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman’s February budget, will run until FY 2039‑40 and aims to increase domestic container production capacity by about ten‑fold, targeting 750,000 twenty‑foot equivalent units (TEUs) per year.

Key features of the CMPS:
- **Interest Subvention (ISA)**: ₹859 crore will be earmarked to provide a 3 % per annum interest subsidy on term loans for setting up new greenfield plants or expanding existing facilities.
- **Operational Expenditure Assistance (OEA)**: ₹8,891 crore will support operational costs for containers manufactured to global shipping standards and sold by eligible manufacturers.
- **Testing & Certification Support**: ₹150 crore will fund common testing facilities such as dynamic longitudinal impact testing.

The scheme is projected to create roughly 3,000 direct jobs and over 50,000 indirect jobs, while also benefiting ancillary sectors like corner castings, specialised steel, wooden frames, and paints. By bridging the cost gap between Indian and Chinese containers—$1,700 for a Chinese TEU versus $2,200‑$2,400 for an Indian one—the government hopes to position India as a global export hub for quality shipping containers.

Industry response has been positive. Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone has expressed interest in building containers in India, and Danish shipping line Maersk placed its first order with Indian manufacturer DCM Containers and Engineering earlier this year.

**How to verify**: The scheme details are published in the Cabinet’s press release and can be cross‑checked with the Ministry of Commerce and Industry’s official website. Companies seeking assistance should consult the scheme guidelines released by the Ministry.
